summary: A 1937 L-4 cab on a 10-foot log tower in the Bitterroot National Forest, restored in 2003 by a ski club with Forest Service staff, reached by a two-mile pack trail.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14x14 ft wood frame with pyramidal roof, on a 10-ft log tower; 1931-pattern designed by Clyde Fickes

access.note: Remote. The only access is a two-mile pack trail on Bitterroot National Forest land. No source says the lookout is open for climbing or overnight use.

visit.trail_note: Two-mile pack trail, the only access per the nomination. The register says locals find the site popular for summer hikes and winter ski-ins.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com's 'presently abandoned' describes staffing, not the structure. The register's 2003 restoration and the nomination's description of an intact building show the cab is still standing.

notes_for_editor: Built year (1937) and L-4 design agree across sources, so confidence on those is high. Current condition is the weak point: no source found is dated after the 2003 restoration, and firelookout.com's 'presently abandoned' note is undated. The nomination's condition description has no date in the text I read. Location: the record uses the NHLR point (45.83737, -114.28933); the RIDB point (45.82449, -114.29445) in the record is about 1.5 km away. Not resolved; a human should check which point is right. Elevation: 7,688 ft (NHLR) vs 7,753 ft (firelookout.com); the record's 2343.3 m follows NHLR. NRHP listing date not confirmed: I did not read the NPGallery listing record for a date; search snippets suggest 2018 but are unverified, so no listing-date event was written. Staffing ended 'mid-1980s' (approximate year 1985). The 1958 start of the staff list is the first name listed on firelookout.com; staff names are deliberately not reproduced.
